links.outcome: Diagnostic reasoning score: physicians with GPT-4 vs conventional resources, and GPT-4 alone
links.effect: Physicians with GPT-4 scored 76.3% vs 73.7% (adjusted difference 1.6 points, 95% CI -4.4 to 7.6; p=0.60). GPT-4 alone scored 15.5 points higher than the conventional resources group (p=0.03).
links.quote: GPT-4 alone scored 15.5 percentage points (95% CI 1.5 to 29, p=0.03) higher than the conventional resources group.

links.outcome: Human-AI team performance versus standalone LLM performance on diagnostic reasoning
links.effect: Access to GPT-4 did not significantly improve physician reasoning (difference 1.6 points, p=0.60), while GPT-4 alone outperformed both physician groups by 15.5 points (p=0.03).
links.quote: GPT-4 alone demonstrated higher performance than both physician groups, suggesting opportunities for further improvement in physician-AI collaboration in clinical practice.

screen.reason: Randomized clinical vignette trial evaluating the effect of providing an LLM (GPT-4) as a clinical decision support aid to physicians compared to conventional diagnostic resources.

primary.practice: physician use of LLM diagnostic aid vs conventional resources
